h1: The 7 Best Single-Burner Induction Cooktops Under $200, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 portable induction cooktops under $200 from Nuwave, Duxtop and ChangBERT, scored on coil size, temperature control and safety.
summary: The Nuwave Portable Induction Cooktop Diamond with Probe is the best induction cooktop under $200, adding a temperature probe and a 100 to 500 degree F range for under $100. The Duxtop 9610LS is the plain reliable choice, the ChangBERT Commercial is the NSF-certified pick with a 10-hour timer, and the Nuwave Gold Precision has the large 8-inch coil.
intro: The cheapest way to try induction is a single countertop burner, and the trap is thinking all of them heat the same. They do not. The size of the heating coil, the number of temperature steps and whether the pan sits securely matter more than the wattage on the box, because nearly every unit here is 1800W or close to it.

Seven portable burners are ranked below, covering the $50 to $100 and $100 to $200 brackets. Each is scored on coil size, temperature control, safety certifications and extras such as probes and timers. A renewed unit in the search results was left out, since condition varies between sellers.

products.name: Nuwave Portable Induction Cooktop Diamond with Probe
products.verdict: A 100 to 500 degree F cooktop with a temperature probe and a diamond-infused surface.
products.description:
The Nuwave Diamond is a countertop induction burner with a 100 to 500 degree F range, a temperature probe in the box and a diamond-infused surface. It sits in the $50 to $100 bracket.

The probe is what lifts it. Instead of guessing from the pan temperature, you can set a target for what is inside the pot, which suits custard, candy and sous-vide-style work. A range topping out at 500 degrees F is plenty for pan-frying, though it stops short of the 575 offered by pricier Nuwaves. The diamond-infused surface is promoted as tougher against scratches, a claim worth taking with a grain of salt but harmless.

Buy it if you want precision on a budget. Skip it if you plan to sear steaks at very high heat.
products.idealFor: Cooks who want precise temperature control.
products.skipIf: You sear at the highest heat.

products.name: Duxtop 9610LS Portable Induction Cooktop
products.verdict: An 1800W burner with 20 preset temperature settings in a black finish.
products.description:
The Duxtop 9610LS delivers 1800W through a countertop burner with 20 preset temperature settings. It is a plain, widely sold design.

Twenty presets give finer steps than a handful of power dials, and 1800W is the ceiling for a standard 15A household outlet. It ranks second because it offers no probe or extras, only a solid basic cooktop. Duxtop is among the best-known names in the category, so spare knowledge and owner advice are easy to find.

Buy it if you want a no-surprise induction burner. Skip it if you want a probe or an NSF label.
cons: Costs more than the Nuwave Diamond
products.idealFor: Anyone who wants a straightforward burner.

products.name: ChangBERT Commercial Grade Induction Cooktop
products.verdict: NSF certified, 1800W, with an 8-inch coil, a 10-hour timer and a stainless steel body.
products.description:
The ChangBERT Commercial Grade cooktop is NSF certified, rated 1800W, has an 8-inch heating coil, a 10-hour timer and a stainless steel body.

NSF certification means it has been evaluated against food-equipment sanitation and construction standards, which matters in a food truck, a church kitchen or a small cafe. The 10-hour timer suits slow simmering and holding. It ranks third because the extras are aimed at commercial users, and a home cook is paying for certification they may not need.

Buy it if you cook for customers or want a tough stainless body. Skip it if you only need basic home cooking.
cons: Commercial features may be wasted at home
products.skipIf: Certification does not matter to you.

products.name: Nuwave Gold Precision Induction Cooktop
products.verdict: A large 8-inch heating coil with precision temperature control, under $100.
products.description:
The Nuwave Gold Precision is a portable burner with a large 8-inch heating coil and precision temperature control.

Coil size shapes how evenly a pan heats: a larger coil covers more of the base and reduces hot spots in a wide skillet. It ranks fourth because the listing omits a temperature range and wattage, so the precision claim cannot be checked. At its price, it is still the cheapest way to get a big coil.

Buy it if you cook in wide pans and want even heat. Skip it if you want a temperature probe.
products.idealFor: Skillet cooking that needs even heat.

products.name: Nuwave Precision Induction Cooktop
products.verdict: A 10.25-inch shatter-resistant ceramic glass top with precision temperature settings.
products.description:
The Nuwave Precision has a 10.25-inch shatter-resistant ceramic glass surface and precision temperature settings.

The broad glass top gives space for a large pan and is easy to wipe. It ranks fifth because the listing gives little detail on temperature range, wattage or coil size, which makes it harder to separate from the Gold Precision. The shatter-resistant glass is welcome, since dropped pans are the usual cause of cracks.

Buy it if you want a large, easy-clean surface. Skip it if you need published figures.
products.skipIf: You want a listed temperature range.

products.name: Duxtop 9600LS Portable Induction Cooktop
products.verdict: The silver version of the same 1800W, 20-preset Duxtop design.
products.description:
The Duxtop 9600LS is an 1800W countertop burner with 20 preset temperature settings in silver.

It matches the 9610LS on every listed spec, so the choice between them comes down to finish and price on the day. Silver shows fingerprints less than black but picks up grease streaks. It ranks sixth because it adds nothing new to the Duxtop below it.

Buy it if you like the silver look or it is cheaper. Skip it if you want a probe or NSF mark.
products.idealFor: Buyers who prefer a silver finish.
products.skipIf: You want any feature beyond the basics.

products.name: ChangBERT Enhanced Portable Induction Cooktop
products.verdict: 1800W with one-click max power, a large coil and low-noise operation.
products.description:
The ChangBERT Enhanced offers 1800W with a one-click max power button, a large heating coil, NSF certification and low-noise operation.

One-click max power helps when you need a fast boil, and quiet running matters in a small kitchen. It ranks last because it costs more than the Nuwave units while offering less precision control, and the listing gives no temperature range.

Buy it if you want quick boiling and a certified body. Skip it if you want fine temperature steps.
products.idealFor: Fast boiling in a quiet kitchen.

whatMatters.detail: Induction heats the part of the pan that sits above the coil. An 8-inch coil covers more of a wide skillet than a 6.5-inch coil, so food browns more evenly. Check the coil diameter in the listing.
Presets in 20 or more steps give finer control than a few power dials. A listed range, such as 100 to 500 degrees F, tells you how low and how high it goes. Missing figures mean less control.
A probe measures food rather than the pan, which is better for custards, sauces and candy. The Nuwave Diamond includes one. It turns an induction cooktop into a more precise tool.
NSF marks indicate the unit was evaluated for food-equipment standards. It matters in commercial kitchens and gives a home cook extra confidence in the build. Two ChangBERT models carry it.
Only magnetic pans heat on induction. If a magnet clings firmly to the base, it will work. Thin or warped pans may rattle or heat unevenly.

faq.q: Is a single-burner induction cooktop enough?
faq.a: For one or two people, yes. It heats faster than electric coils and gives gas-like control. If you routinely use several pots at once, consider a double or a built-in.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with portable induction?
faq.a: Using the wrong pan. Aluminium and glass do not work, and thin pans can warp. Check that a magnet clings to the base before buying cookware.

faq.q: Is the Duxtop worth it over the Nuwave Diamond?
faq.a: Only if you prefer its preset layout and brand. The Nuwave Diamond adds a probe and costs less, though its range stops at 500 degrees F.
No. These plug into a standard 120V outlet. Avoid sharing the circuit with other high-power appliances like a microwave.
Let it cool, then wipe the glass with a damp cloth. For stuck-on food use a ceramic cooktop cleaner. Keep the vents free of dust.

faq.q: Why does it make a noise?
faq.a: A faint hum or fan sound is normal, and thin pans can buzz. Heavier, flat-bottomed pans are quieter. The ChangBERT Enhanced lists low-noise operation.

finalTake: The Nuwave Portable Induction Cooktop Diamond with Probe is the best induction cooktop under $200, offering a 100 to 500 degree F range and a probe at a sub-$100 price. The Duxtop 9610LS is the reliable plain choice, and the ChangBERT Commercial is the NSF-certified pick for food service. Make sure your pans pass the magnet test before you commit.
